text: Acceleration is the rate at which velocity changes with time. An object accelerates when its speed changes, when its direction changes, or when both change.
embed_text: Acceleration is the rate at which velocity changes with time. An object accelerates when its speed changes, when its direction changes, or when both change.

text: Velocity is a vector quantity that describes how fast an object moves and the direction of its motion. Speed is the magnitude of velocity and carries no direction.
embed_text: Velocity is a vector quantity that describes how fast an object moves and the direction of its motion. Speed is the magnitude of velocity and carries no direction.

text: Displacement is the change in position of an object. Unlike distance travelled, displacement depends only on the starting and ending positions.

text: Newton's first law states that an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed, unless a net force acts on it.
embed_text: Newton's first law states that an object at rest stays at rest, and an object in motion keeps moving in a straight line at constant speed, unless a net force acts on it.

text: Newton's second law relates the net force on an object to its mass and its acceleration, and is usually written as force equals mass times acceleration.
embed_text: Newton's second law relates the net force on an object to its mass and its acceleration, and is usually written as force equals mass times acceleration.

text: Newton's third law states that when one body exerts a force on a second body, the second body exerts a force of equal magnitude and opposite direction on the first.
embed_text: Newton's third law states that when one body exerts a force on a second body, the second body exerts a force of equal magnitude and opposite direction on the first.

text: Friction is a contact force that opposes the relative motion of two surfaces. Its magnitude depends on the normal force pressing the surfaces together and on the materials involved.

text: Work is done when a force moves an object through a distance along the direction of that force. Work transfers energy into or out of a system.
embed_text: Work is done when a force moves an object through a distance along the direction of that force. Work transfers energy into or out of a system.

text: Kinetic energy is the energy an object has because of its motion. It grows with the mass of the object and with the square of its speed.
